pr_title: reverseproxy: Only retry responses for expressions that use response data
pr_body:
Closes #8166

Since #7569 every `lb_retry_match` set containing an `expression` is evaluated against the upstream response. An expression that only tests the request, like `{http.request.method} == "POST"`, matched every successful response, so the request was sent again to the next upstreams and the client got a 502 when retries ran out.

Response retries now apply only to expressions that reference response placeholders (`{rp.*}`, which the Caddyfile adapts to `{http.reverse_proxy.*}`). Other expressions are request conditions again, as before v2.11.3. All the examples from #7569 reference `{rp.*}` and behave as before.

Test: `TestRequestOnlyExpressionDoesNotRetryResponses` sends a POST through two healthy upstreams with that expression. Without the change it returns a 502 (`ContentLength=7 with Body length 0` on the retry); with it the upstream is hit once and the 200 body comes through. `go test ./...` passes, including the existing retry_match unit and integration tests.

Manual check with the Caddyfile from the issue: v2.11.7 answers the POST with 502 after three upstream hits; with the change it returns the backend's 200 after one hit.

## Assistance Disclosure

Claude Code (Claude Opus) helped write this patch and its test. I reviewed every line, and I ran the test before and after the change and the manual check above myself.
commit_message:
reverseproxy: Only retry responses for expressions that use response data (#8168)
* reverseproxy: Only retry responses for expressions that use response data

Since #7569 every lb_retry_match set with an expression is evaluated against
upstream responses. An expression that only tests the request, such as
{http.request.method} == "POST", then matched every successful response:
the request was sent again to the next upstreams and the client got a 502
once retries ran out. Only treat expressions referencing {rp.*} placeholders
as response conditions.

* reverseproxy: Only count placeholders set from the response as response data

* reverseproxy: Read response placeholders from the checked expression

The expression matcher records the placeholder names its checked CEL
expression reads, so retry_match finds direct ph() calls and ignores
escaped placeholder text in string literals. A placeholder name only
known at evaluation time counts as response data.

* reverseproxy: Match response placeholder names exactly

Only the header placeholders are matched by prefix now, and both
upstream latency placeholders are listed. MatchExpression.Placeholders
returns a copy, so callers cannot change the provisioned matcher.
task_text:
# reverseproxy: lb_retry_match with a request-only expression retries successful responses (502 since v2.11.3)

### Issue Details

Since v2.11.3, an `lb_retry_match` block with an `expression` that only tests the request makes every successful upstream response retryable. The request is sent again to the next upstreams (a POST arrives with an empty body after the first attempt), and once the retries run out the client gets a `502`. A GET gets a `200` with an empty body.

Version: v2.11.7 (release binary) and master at 700d6032. v2.11.2 behaves as expected.

Caddyfile (two backends that always answer 200 on :9001 and :9002):

```
{
	admin off
	auto_https off
}
:9000 {
	reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:9001 127.0.0.1:9002 {
		lb_policy round_robin
		lb_retries 2
		lb_retry_match {
			expression `{http.request.method} == "POST"`
		}
	}
}
```

```
$ curl -i -d order=1 localhost:9000/order
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Server: Caddy
Content-Length: 0
```

The backends log three POSTs for that one request: the first with body `order=1`, the next two with an empty body:

```
HIT :9002 POST /order body=b'order=1'
HIT :9001 POST /order body=b''
HIT :9002 POST /order body=b''
```

With v2.11.2 the same request gets the backend's `200` and the backend sees it once.

Expected: the docs describe `lb_retry_match` as restricting "with which requests retries are allowed" when the round-trip failed, using request matcher syntax, so a successful response should be passed through.

Cause: #7569 evaluates every retry_match set that contains an `expression` against the upstream response (`modules/caddyhttp/reverseproxy/reverseproxy.go`, the `matcherSetHasExpressionMatcher` loop after the round-trip). An expression without `{rp.*}` placeholders matches every response for a matching request, so it is treated as a retryable response.

I have a small patch with a test (only treat expressions that reference `{rp.*}` placeholders as response conditions; other expressions keep their earlier meaning) and can open a PR if this sounds right.

### Assistance Disclosure

AI used

### If AI was used, describe the extent to which it was used.

Claude Code (Claude Opus) helped write the reproduction, the patch and its test. I reviewed every line and re-ran the steps above myself.
